transcript:
Header: 2028-03-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SRE); Raj Patel (CrestlineFin), Sofia Morales (Crestline), Ethan Clarke (Crestline CTO)
---
Summary (auto): quick wins on TTFT, need kernel deep-dive and larger bench.

00:00 Raj: hey everyone, thanks for doing the weekly, we shipped the small client changes yesterday, we saw some initial improvements but wanted to go over the numbers.
00:12 Maya: thanks Raj, yeah Liam and I will walk through what we measured and then we want to flag the remaining infra things.
00:25 Liam: ok quick context — baseline last week was average TTFT ~180ms with p95 ~420ms when using non-streaming batch exec and default kernel selection. After switching to streaming-first path and enabling kernel pinning on the staging pool we see median TTFT ~88-95ms, p95 down to ~210ms. Those are rough numbers, medium transcription here.
00:48 Sofia: when you say kernel pinning, can you restate what you did? I thought kernel selection was automatic in the runtime.
00:56 Liam: yeah good question — by default the runtime picks kernels per op and can switch on the fly. We forced a static selection to avoid runtime branch overhead and avoid some slow fallbacks. It reduces jitter. On our side we disabled the dynamic selector for matmul and attention for the short-seq path.
01:15 Raj: hmm that makes sense. Are we seeing any throughput regressions when pinning?
01:20 Priya: on our runs throughput stayed flat for the request rates you tested (up to 120 rps), we actually saw slightly better GPU utilization due to less tail variance.
01:34 Ethan: any impact to token accuracy or decoding determinism? We need to ensure results don't degrade for compliance.
01:41 Liam: no functional change, same model weights and quant config. We did try a lightweight 4-bit quant on a variant and it introduced some small soft-safety issues in a handful of prompts, so we didn't enable that for the main run.
01:58 Maya: quick note — Crestline's production workload has a heavy short-seq tail (mostly 16-64 tokens), Raj if you can send the exact percentiles that will help us tune the batching/windowing.
02:10 Raj: sure, I'll export the sequence-length histogram from prod tomorrow.
02:16 Sofia: about streaming — we toggled streaming in our client and the first token latency improved but end-to-end time went up a little in some cases — what's the tradeoff here?
02:28 Liam: yep streaming reduces TTFT by returning the first tokens as soon as decoding begins; total completion time can increase slightly because we break up batches earlier. We adjusted the streaming chunk-size to 8 tokens which gave us a good middle ground. Also enabling prefix/KV caching reduced repeated context recompute and helped overall.
02:52 Raj: how did KV cache affect p95?
02:56 Liam: on staging with a realistic hit rate (~35-40%) p95 moved from ~210ms to ~170ms in the mixed profile. If we can increase hit rate to 60% it'll be even better.
03:12 Sofia: do we need any changes to our infra to support KV cache? Anything around memory or eviction?
03:18 Priya: you need to provision a bit more RAM on the inference nodes for the cache windows; we recommended a 10% headroom. Eviction policy defaults work fine for your typical session lengths.
03:32 Ethan: kernel choices — you mentioned matmul and fused attention kernels. Are these our custom kernels or vendor ones?
03:38 Liam: it's a mix. We use vendor-optimized cuBLAS/cuDNN where it wins, but we also have a custom fused-attention kernel optimized for short sequences. For some sequence lengths the fused kernel is faster, for others cuBLAS with tiled matmul is better. That's why we want to pin per-target distribution.
03:56 Raj: can you produce a per-sequence-length latency table so we can see crossover points?
04:01 Liam: yes, that's on our action item list — per-kernel p50/p95/p99 by sequence length.
04:09 Maya: one more real-world ask — we noticed spikes during high concurrency test last week; was that related to dynamic kernel switching?
04:17 Liam: likely, yes — the dynamic selector sometimes probes fallbacks under contention which increases jitter. Pinning removed those probes. We still see some queuing at the runtime input stage at >200 rps; we'll look at batching window thresholds.
04:33 Raj: any changes needed around SSO or security for the staging runs? We haven't touched the VPC connector.
04:39 Maya: no, staging is unchanged, private deployment knobs are still the same. We only changed runtime flags.
04:45 Sofia: for the 10k benchmark, do you want us to replicate prod TLS settings or can we run a simplified non-TLS path?
04:52 Priya: simplified is fine for latency-focused runs; we recommend doing one run with prod TLS to validate overhead. But initial run without TLS gives clearer kernel-level signal.
05:06 Ethan: what's the expected improvement if we increase KV hit rate to 60% and keep streaming chunk 8?
05:12 Liam: conservatively p95 could go to ~120-140ms, median to ~60-70ms. That's contingent on the sequence mix.
05:22 Raj: good — to summarize next steps, Crestline will send sequence histogram and run 10k synthetic requests; Redwood will share per-kernel breakdown and trimmed benchmark outputs.
05:33 Maya: yup we'll also schedule the deep-dive with infra to walk through kernel internals and potential runtime patching.
05:40 Sofia: one more quick note — procurement asked about pricing for dedicated vs hosted if we want to move to Dedicated after POC. Maya: we'll send a pricing outline in the follow-up email.
05:52 Ethan: ok thanks all, anything else?
05:55 Raj: no, appreciate it.
05:57 Maya: thanks team, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
06:00 call end

Action recap (spoken): Liam to push kernel breakdown and histograms; Raj to share sequence distribution; Sofia to enable KV cache on staging and report hit rate; Redwood to schedule kernel deep-dive.
